description: The final series without final/0047 "perf(field_t): is_normalized compares raw limbs": 75 commits (0001-0002 harness, 73 optimisations). That commit assumed field elements are held in [0, 2p), true natively but not in WASM (R = 2^261, 29-bit limbs), so the WASM build emitted 2 extra kernel-circuit rows and its proofs failed verification. First series with WASM numbers.

machine.cpu: Intel Xeon, family 6 model 173 (Granite Rapids), 4 vCPUs, AVX-512 IFMA (IFMA kernels active)

correctness.notes: On the IFMA VM (final2-ifma-vm.md): check_identical 14/14 IDENTICAL with IFMA on and with BB_FIELD_NO_IFMA=1 BB_MSM_NO_IFMA=1; stock bb.js 7.0.0-nightly.20261009 verifies all 14 in both modes; unmodified native bb verify 14/14 (tampered rejected). On the no-IFMA coordinator VM (sources/final2/): check_identical.txt: 14/14 IDENTICAL; verify_stock_bbjs.txt: stock npm bb.js 7.0.0-nightly.20261009 verifies all 14 flows, tampered rejected, VKs equal; verify_native_unmodified.txt: unmodified native bb verify 14/14, tampered rejected. WASM: all 25 benchmark runs proved by the final2 WASM build verified by bb.js's bundled (unmodified) WASM verifier, tampered proofs rejected. Unit tests: pending.

summary.notes: All 14 flows x 3 reps on the AVX-512 IFMA VM, interleaved, time = min wall, RAM = max peak RSS of bb; the headline flow row is the dedicated min-of-7 run.

standards.machine_note: AVX-512 IFMA VM: headline min of 7 (time min, peak RSS max); other token flows from the 14-flow x 3-rep run. WASM columns: no-IFMA VM, stock bb.js (wasm_bench.md)

caveats: WASM peak RSS is dominated by the linear-memory high-water mark, which never shrinks, so the native RAM savings barely carry over to WASM (headline WASM RAM −0.5%).

Headline and all-flows numbers are from an AVX-512 IFMA VM (Granite Rapids), the hardware the IFMA kernels target. The other cards were measured on a VM without IFMA; final2 on that VM is under "Also measured": headline −30.8% time, −27.0% RAM. WASM numbers are from the no-IFMA VM.
On the progress chart final2 uses its no-IFMA run, which has its own unmodified baseline (an earlier run than the other milestone cards, same VM type), so ratios are comparable but seconds are not.
